messages:
maya: Heads-up — I've been thinking about delegated config ownership for per-route quotas + telemetry handoff. Need a proposal we can iterate on in the console and API.

sam: +1, we should let product teams own their route quotas but require a telemetry mapping so platform can detect regressions.

leo: Quick Q — do we mean full write access to runtime flags, or scoped ownership (only specific keys under /routes/<id/>)?

maya: Scoped only. Owners get a namespace like routes/<route_id>/overrides. Platform keeps global defaults and a read-only history. We need audit + an approval path for risky changes.

anya: Approval path = canary window + telemetry gate? e.g., owner creates override -> it goes to shadow mode for X hours -> compare key signals -> auto-promote if ok or rollback.

sam: Exactly. Telemetry signals we care about: p50/p95 latency delta, error rate, token cost per request, rejection/quotas triggered. We should centralize the signal mapping so teams can't accidentally hide regressions.

leo: Can we make the shadow mode non-invasive: route receives both configs but only metrics are recorded for the shadow path (no user-facing change) — that's how we validate.

maya: Prefer shadow path for safety. Also want TTL for temporary overrides: owners can set override_ttl (minutes) that auto-expires. Default 24h.

sam: Sketching the API: POST /v1/routes/:id/overrides with body:
```json
{
  "owner": "team-name",
  "key": "quota.max_per_minute",
  "value": 500,
  "mode": "shadow|active",
  "override_ttl": 1440,
  "canary_window_minutes": 30,
  "telemetry_mapping": ["latency.p95","errors.rate"]
}
```

anya: A few notes: 1) telemetry_mapping should accept named buckets so console can plot them automatically, 2) we need server-side validation to reject mappings we don't support, 3) owners should be able to request a manual approval which pings platform-oncall.

leo: For the console UX: when a team creates an override show an impact preview (simulated QPS) + baseline & shadow comparisons. Also show a single-click rollback during the canary.

devops-bot: deploy-check:shadow-deploy created for route=api-payments override_id=ovr-237111-1 mode=shadow ttl=30m

maya: Good call. For telemetry handoff: platform will own the canonical metric definitions and alert thresholds. Team-level mapping maps local metric name -> canonical metric id. That way alerts and regression detectors can run consistently.

sam: How about authorization model: teams with "route_admin" role can create shadow overrides; "route_owner" can promote to active only after a 24h cool-down or explicit manual approval? Prevents accidental flips.

anya: I like manual approval for critical keys (billing, quotas, routing). We should tag keys as "sensitive" in the schema. UI should require 2-step confirmation for sensitive promotions.

leo: Edge case: overlapping overrides from multiple teams for same route. Suggest we implement a priority field (higher priority wins) and platform UI shows effective config with stack trace of contributions.

maya: Yes — show provenance: default <- teamA override (shadow) <- teamB override (active). And provide an audit diff button.

sam: Telemetry gating rule prototype: 
- Collect shadow vs baseline for canary_window
- Compute delta for each canonical metric
- If delta exceeds threshold for any metric (config-defined), mark failed and auto-roll back
- Send annotated alert to owner + platform-oncall

anya: We need a lightweight DSL for thresholds, example: 
```yaml
metrics:
  - id: latency.p95
    threshold_pct: 15
  - id: errors.rate
    threshold_absolute: 0.01
```

leo: Implementation note: use the existing metrics pipeline (temporal windowing) and tag canary traces with override_id. Shouldn't be too invasive.

maya: Ops question — do we allow owners to bypass gating for emergencies? If so, require audit note and 2FA confirmation.

sam: Yes but only platform-admins or postmortem-required bypass. Record the reason.

devops-bot: audit:override-create override_id=ovr-237111-1 actor=maya mode=shadow ttl=30m

anya: Next steps: 1) design API + schema 2) add console wireframes for preview & provenance 3) implement shadow path tagging in runtime 4) telemetry gating prototype 5) run experiment with payments team.

maya: I'll draft a PR with API schema and a short design doc. @sam can you take telemetry gating prototype? @leo can you scope runtime tagging work? @anya will do console mocks.

sam: On it.

leo: I'll start a spike tomorrow.

anya: Will post mocks by EOD Friday.

maya: Thanks all :thumbsup:
